First, recall that the sum 1+2+…+n = n(n+1)/2. The expression (n(n+1)/2)^2 is a perfect fourth power if and only if n(n+1)/2 is a perfect square, since squaring a perfect square gives a fourth power. n and n+1 are coprime, so their product divided by 2 is a square only when one is a square and the other is twice a square.
